subject.title: [Feature]: Support custom HTTP headers on CLI WebSocket connections

question: Should Gateway CLI accept custom WebSocket HTTP headers, and which CLI/env/config sources, precedence, and credential safeguards should become the supported public contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear and ws supports request options, but arbitrary headers change the proxy-auth boundary and may carry credentials, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Approve a narrow secret-safe contract
options.body: Add header forwarding through maintainer-approved sources only, with SecretInput/env substitution, reserved-header filtering, redaction, TLS guidance, docs, and tests for fresh and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Limit support to per-invocation CLI headers
options.body: Support only repeatable explicit CLI headers first, avoiding durable config/env persistence at the cost of CI and automation ergonomics.

options.title: Decline core header support
options.body: Keep SSH, Tailscale, and local proxy workflows as the supported paths and document reverse-proxy header injection as outside the Gateway CLI contract.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow secret-safe contract
recommendation.body: Add header forwarding through maintainer-approved sources only, with SecretInput/env substitution, reserved-header filtering, redaction, TLS guidance, docs, and tests for fresh and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter owns the closest Gateway/WebSocket and mobile custom-header decisions and is the best available security-boundary decision owner from history.
